answer: Coordination Inlet Pricing. Each epoch, agents must route all intra-coalition messages through a shared inlet whose capacity is fixed per epoch; fee per message rises with the square of distinct senders seen, not volume. A sybil cluster flooding the inlet pays convexly more per added identity while honest low-coordination agents pay near zero. The reef of accumulated per-sender history makes fresh clones start at the highest marginal rate, and each new identity triggers a ripple that raises the cluster’s own next-message price.
